lines.text: Time Capsule Unearthed During
Dorm Renovation
Construction crews renovating Murdoch Hall have discovered a
time capsule buried by students in the year 1896, sparking
excitement across campus.
Inside were letters, photographs, and a campus map showing
buildings long gone. "It's like stepping into the past," said
archivist Dana Wells, who catalogued the items. Students lined
up to view the capsule's contents, marveling at the artifacts.
"Seeing their hopes and dreams—it's inspiring," said
junior Malik Johnson.
The university will host an exhibit next month featuring the
capsule's contents alongside reflections from current students,
some of whom have expressed interest in contributing to a new
capsule, creating a bridge between the past and the present.
"It's a reminder of how much has changed—and how
much hasn't," Wells added.
The discovery has sparked conversations about campus
traditions and the importance of preserving history, turning a
routine renovation into a moment of shared pride and curiosity.
